summary: TechCrunch's running, month-by-month list of known tech layoffs in 2023, from January through December, covering big firms like Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta as well as many startups. The industry lost more than 240,000 jobs in 2023, about 50% more than in 2022, as companies shifted from growth to efficiency amid stubborn market conditions. Each entry gives the company, the announcement date, and the size or percentage of the cut where known.
one_line: TechCrunch's monthly-updated list of 2023 tech layoffs, tallying over 240,000 job cuts across big tech and startups, higher than 2022's total.
key_facts: The tech industry lost more than 240,000 jobs in 2023, about 50% higher than the previous year.
Layoffs.fyi's running total for 2023 based on full months to date was 224,503, exceeding the total for all of 2022.
Layoffs slowed in summer and fall 2023 but appeared to be ramping up again by year-end.
Alphabet announced on January 21 that it would lay off 6% of its global workforce, equating to 12,000 employees, including Area 120 and Intrinsic.
Amazon announced on January 5 it would eliminate more than 18,000 roles, followed by 9,000 more in March, totaling 27,000 or 8% of its corporate workforce.
Microsoft announced 10,000 layoffs on January 18, and cut additional jobs in July; it laid off 559 workers in Bellevue and Redmond on March 27.
Meta cut about 21,000 people since November, including 10,000 announced in March (plus about 5,000 open roles) and about 6,000 on May 24.
Salesforce announced on January 4 it would cut 10% of its workforce, impacting more than 7,000 employees.
Nokia announced on October 19 it would cut up to 14,000 jobs, or 16% of its workforce.
Accenture announced on March 23 a plan to cut 19,000 jobs, or 2.5% of its workforce.
Cruise announced a cut of 900 employees, or 24% of its workforce, in a December 14 email from new president and CTO Mo Elshenawy.
Byju's announced on September 26 it would cut 5,000 jobs, having eliminated more than 10,000 positions in two years.
Spotify announced about 1,500 job cuts on December 4, its third round of layoffs in 2023.
Epic Games announced on September 28 it was laying off 16% of its workforce, amounting to 870 people.
SmileDirectClub shut down three months after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing $900 million of debt.
